title: Forward-compatible circuit-breaker for embeddings+reranker: error mapping and iterator semantics
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Legacy clients rely on a mix of cursor semantics, HTTP codes, and streaming iterator behaviors for embeddings+rerank flows. As we introduce streaming, tool-calls, and structured outputs in the same surface area, small endpoint changes cascade to production regressions for customers using older SDKs or home-grown clients.

Objective: Deliver a forward-compatible 'circuit-breaker' compatibility layer that: (1) provides strict error-code mapping between new internal error taxonomy and legacy HTTP+cursor expectations, (2) normalizes pagination/cursor semantics across streaming and non-streaming flows, and (3) exposes a minimal runtime toggle so hosts can opt into strict-parity mode while we ramp integrations. The compatibility layer must be observable, testable, and reversible for canary rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Define canonical mapping doc: new_error_code => legacy_http_status + error_type header
Cursor semantics spec published that covers: per-page cursors, stable offsets, tombstones and idempotent retry hints
Compatibility layer implemented as an API gateway module behind a feature flag 'parity.circuit_breaker'
Integration tests that run legacy client vectors (4 popular SDK patterns) against parity mode and baseline mode with 0 regressions for pagination and error handling
Telemetry dashboards tracking: parity-enabled request rate, error-mapping incidents, cursor-mismatch errors, and client-side timeouts
Rollback path documented: steps to disable parity flag and flush sticky routing
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with Eng and Design. Agreed to target both streaming and non-streaming iterator contracts; product will own acceptance matrices.
2025-02-18: Engineering spike completed. Prototype gateway module can inject 'X-Compatibility-Error' header and translate 5 canonical error classes.
2025-02-24: Design review. UX for structured output errors (tool-calls) will surface a "legacy_code" block when parity mode is enabled; design provided fallback render examples.
2025-02-28: Created integration test harness to replay recorded legacy client traces (from support logs) against local parity gateway.
2025-03-02: Security reviewed data flows; no secret materialization in gateways. Performance baseline shows 6% p50 latency overhead in parity mode; engineering investigating optimization.
2025-03-02: Merged routing config PR to staging behind feature flag (ENG-82190).
decisions: Use header-based mapping for non-fatal error hints rather than changing payload shapes to minimize client parsing churn.
Implement cursor normalization at the gateway by translating streaming chunk offsets into stable opaque cursors for legacy clients.
Expose parity mode as a per-customer toggle in Console and as an 'X-Parity-Mode' request override for self-serve tests.
Prioritize error mapping parity for the top 6 subclasses observed in production (rate_limit, model_unavailable, quota_exceeded, transient_gpu_error, malformed_request, internal_assertion).
technical_notes: Gateway will run translation middleware in the dedicated routing tier to avoid touching downstream serving nodes.
Cursor translation strategy: maintain a short-lived mapping table (TTL 12h) keyed by (request_id, stream_segment_id) with opaque token returned to legacy clients.
To minimize memory, tombstone cursors use a deterministic hash + segment timestamp; table pruning will be windowed during low traffic.
Backpressure: when streaming to a client expecting page-based responses, gateway will buffer up to 2 pages-worth of tokens and expose 'more_available' boolean in legacy cursor payload.
Metrics emitted: parity.error_map.<class> counters, parity.cursor_hit_rate, parity.latency.overhead.p50/p95, parity.rollback.count
migration_steps: Stage 1 (canary): Enable parity for internal test customers and replay historical traces. Run parity-only test suite.
Stage 2 (pilot): Enable parity for 10% of eligible external customers; monitor error surfacing dashboards for 48h.
Stage 3 (gradual rollout): Ramp to 100% of legacy-tier customers over 7 days if no regressions; keep feature off for new SDK cohorts by default.
Fallback: Toggle off 'parity.circuit_breaker' and flush routing table; provide a 5-minute maintenance window for clients to reconnect.
test_plan: Unit tests for error mapping logic with 120+ cases covering canonical and edge errors.
Integration suite that replays 50k legacy client session traces across streaming/non-streaming permutations.
Chaos test: inject transient model_unavailable errors and verify gateway produces legacy retry-hint headers and idempotency-safe cursors.
Performance test: compare p50/p95 for parity ON vs OFF under mixed load (50% streaming, 50% batch embeddings).
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated deployment to routing cluster A/B. Canary for 2 hours with internal traffic, then 24h internal stress run.
Enable pilot on pilot-customer list and observe for 72h. Require SLO: parity.cursor_mismatch_rate < 0.1% and parity.error_mismatch_rate < 0.2%.
Provide opt-in switch in Console under 'API compatibility' with audit logging for toggles.
Post-rollout: 7 day watch with on-call eng and PM slack channel active; run customer outreach for any anomalies.
risks: Memory pressure in routing tier if cursor mapping TTL is too long for high churn workloads.
Inadvertent behavior differences for edge-case streaming sequences where multi-tool calls interleave with embeddings responses.
Per-request latency regression that could breach Dedicated latency SLOs if parity enabled broadly without optimizations.
Potential for clients to rely on parity headers and delay SDK upgrades, complicating long-term deprecation plans.
